lines.text: It's really important that shared credentials are not common practice in your organization, that every person has their own unique credentials.
Anything that does require shared credentials would be a service.
Otherwise, it's going to be extremely hard to figure out some sort of attribution.
When a security event happens, you want to know who, what, when, and where.
And where did it come from?
But if you have shared credentials, you cannot know the who.
That's where you start with authentication at your company.
That's part of that, is eliminating shared credentials, strengthening your password requirements.
That's where you're going to get the most value for your security there.
